summary.text: Don Davis is the Democratic incumbent seeking a third term in North Carolina's 1st Congressional District, now redrawn to lean more Republican. A Snow Hill native, Air Force Academy graduate and Air Force veteran, he was an Air Force ROTC instructor at East Carolina University, mayor of Snow Hill and a North Carolina state senator before his election to Congress in 2022. He is ranking member of the Agriculture Committee's Subcommittee on Commodity Markets, Digital Assets, and Rural Development.

paragraphs.text: Don Davis was born and raised in Snow Hill, North Carolina, where he worked in tobacco fields as a young man; according to his official biography, he still attends and ministers at the church he attended growing up.

He graduated from the U.S. Air Force Academy in 1994 with a bachelor's degree in social sciences, and later earned a master's degree in administration from Central Michigan University, a master's in sociology with a concentration in regional development, and a doctorate in education from East Carolina University.

Davis served eight years on active duty as an Air Force officer; as a first lieutenant he coordinated Air Force One and congressional delegation (CODEL) operations at Andrews Air Force Base and supported military families as a mortuary officer.

He then returned to eastern North Carolina as an assistant professor of Aerospace Studies with East Carolina University's Air Force ROTC Detachment 600, teaching national security affairs, military history and leadership, and describes more than 20 years as an educator.
Davis became the youngest mayor of Snow Hill at age 29 and served seven years.
He was elected to the North Carolina State Senate in 2008 and served 12 years, according to his official biography.
He won the 1st District seat in 2022 after Rep. G. K. Butterfield's retirement and was re-elected in 2024 by a 5,826-vote margin over Laurie Buckhout, who is his opponent again in 2026.

In the House, Davis serves on the Agriculture Committee (as ranking member of the Subcommittee on Commodity Markets, Digital Assets, and Rural Development, appointed in 2025) and the Armed Services Committee (as vice ranking member), and he co-chairs the For Country Caucus.
He lives in Greene County with his wife, Yuvonka; they have three sons, Ryan, Justin and Kyler.
